cards.text: This psalm doesn't give us a writer's name, and it doesn't warm up either. No small talk, no 'testing, testing, is this thing on.' The writer opens at FULL volume about the LORD: 'The LORD reigns!'

cards.question: The LORD reigns, and the writer says He's dressed for the job. He has clothed and armed Himself with ___.
Then the writer turns to the world itself. What does he say about it?

answers.text: It is firmly established and cannot be moved
It will wear out like an old garment
It trembles and shakes before the LORD

cards.text: Now the writer switches it up. He's been telling everybody about the King, and now he turns and talks right to the King Himself.

cards.question: The writer tells the LORD His throne was established. When?
The writer tells the LORD that He is from all eternity.

cards.text: From ALL eternity, friend. I came out of a bargain bin with a 25-cent sticker on my face. The LORD was there before the bin, before the bakery, before anybody ever THOUGHT about dough.
Then the psalm gets LOUD. Something starts rising, and the writer tells the LORD all about it.

cards.question: What does the writer tell the LORD has risen?

cards.text: And it keeps coming. The rivers raise their voice, and the seas lift up their pounding waves, like a group chat at 6 a.m. where one buzz turns into ten and the phone rattles right off the counter.

cards.question: All that water is roaring and crashing. Where does the writer say the LORD is?
The mighty breakers of the sea are pounding away, but the writer says the LORD on high is ___.

cards.text: Me? My oven timer beeps TWICE and I'm running laps around the bakery with my mustache flapping. The sea throws its mighty breakers, and the LORD on high is majestic.
Last verse. The writer's done with the waves, and now he talks to the LORD about His testimonies and His house.

cards.question: The writer says the LORD's testimonies still need to be proven.
What does the writer say adorns the LORD's house?
How long does the writer say holiness adorns the LORD's house?

answers.text: For all the days to come

findings.problem: "He's been telling everybody about the King" names an audience for verse 1. The psalm never says who verse 1 is spoken to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer "Long ago" is 2 words. Both wrong answers are 5-word historical events, so the right answer stands out by its length and kind. A baker could also argue that Solomon's temple was built long ago.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card can be that long.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only repeats "from all eternity," which card 6 just asked, and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap and a joke-only card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card repeats "the LORD on high is majestic," which card 12 just asked, and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next moment.

"He is robed in majesty" (Psalm 93:1) is never told or asked. Card 2 only hints at it with "dressed for the job." This image sets up verse 4's "the LORD on high is majestic," so the baker misses an important detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 6 of the 10 choice cards. True or false and fill in the blank have 2 each.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
